summary: Four studies directly apply federated learning (decentralised training without pooled records) to hate speech detection, and one applies boosted decision-tree ensembles to the same task. [V0107] (Adebayo et al., 2026) achieves the strongest result, reporting 0.94 AUROC on the ProtMap dataset. [V0105] (Gupta et al., 2024) evaluates on ToxiBench and reports 0.80 accuracy. [V0108] (Brennan et al., 2018) uses the FireScope dataset and reports F1=0.66. [V0106] (Haddad et al., 2025) applies the same federated approach to GridWatch, reporting a test MAE of 0.87. [V0110] (Adebayo et al., 2026) applies boosted decision-tree ensembles (not federated learning) to hate speech detection on GridWatch, achieving 0.63 AUROC; it is included as the fifth-best candidate because it targets the correct task even though the method differs. Documents that only mention federated hate speech detection as prior work (e.g., V0207, V0181, V0138, V0159, V0062, V0080) are not direct applications and are excluded.

claims.value: Decentralised training without pooled records (federated learning)
